extracted.intended_audience: authors, illustrators, publishers, and nominators submitting beginning-reader books for the Theodor Seuss Geisel Award
extracted.subtask_description: Terms, eligibility, and evaluative criteria for the Theodor Seuss Geisel Award, which recognizes the most distinguished American book for beginning readers published in English in the U.S. during the preceding year. Includes definitions of 'distinguished', detailed language and illustration expectations, eligibility and procedural submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Theodor Seuss Geisel Award recognizes the author(s) and illustrator(s) of a book for beginning readers who, through their literary and artistic achievements, demonstrate creativity and imagination to engage children in reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award honors both literary and artistic achievements specifically aimed at engaging beginning readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary eligibility — publication locale and language
rubrics_metrics.description: The award shall be given annually to ... an American book for beginning readers published in English in the United States during the preceding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books originally published in other countries are not eligible ('American children’s literature' means that books originally published in other countries are not eligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and functionality for beginning readers
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no limitations as to the character of the book considered except that it will be original and function successfully as a book for beginning readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book must be an original work (reprints and compilations are not eligible) and must work effectively for the target beginning-reader audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author/illustrator residency/citizenship restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Award is restricted to author(s) and illustrator(s) who are citizens or residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-authors and co-illustrators are allowable; awards may be given posthumously to eligible creators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'distinguished'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Distinguished" is defined as: Marked by distinction: noted for significant achievement; Marked by excellence in quality; Marked by conspicuous excellence or eminence; Individually distinct; Providing a stimulating and successful reading experience for the beginning reader containing the kind of plot, sensibility, and rhythm that can carry a child along from start to finish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee should assess overall conspicuous excellence and whether the book provides a stimulating, successful reading experience with suitable plot, sensibility, and rhythm for beginning readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target age/grade and role of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: "Contribution to the body of children’s literature that encourages and supports the beginning reader" indicates the text of a book, which must be directed at readers from pre-K through Grade 2. The book must also contain illustrations, which function as keys or clues to the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee shall consider how text and illustrations work together to support beginning readers (illustrations should be integral, not merely decorative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of writing eligible; ineligible formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee shall consider all forms of writing—fiction, non-fiction, and poetry. Reprints and compilations are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any literary form aimed at beginning readers is acceptable as long as it meets other eligibility and functionality requirements; previously published material compiled/reprinted is excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader experience — subject matter and motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter must be intriguing enough to motivate the child to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the topic/subject engages a beginning reader's interest and motivates independent reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language development and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: New words should be added slowly enough to make learning them a positive experience; Words should be repeated to ensure knowledge retention.; Sentences must be simple and straightforward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate vocabulary introduction pace, beneficial repetition, and sentence simplicity appropriate for pre-K through Grade 2 learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and pacing — chapters and page-turning
rubrics_metrics.description: The book may or may not include short 'chapters'; The plot advances from one page to the next and creates a 'page-turning' dynamic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether structure (including optional short chapters) and narrative momentum sustain a beginning reader's attention and encourage continued reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length constraints (pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a minimum of 24 pages. Books may not be longer than 96 pages;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page count must fall within 24–96 pages to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration quality and function
rubrics_metrics.description: The illustrations must demonstrate the story being told.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether illustrations clearly convey or reinforce the narrative/action and serve as effective 'keys or clues' to the text rather than merely decorative images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall successful reading experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The book creates a successful reading experience, from start to finish;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holistic assessment of coherence, engagement, readability, and whether text + illustration combine to deliver a satisfying beginning-reader experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee consideration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee in its deliberations is to consider only the books eligible for the award, as specified in the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee should strictly apply eligibility rules (publication locale, dates, page limits, originality, creator residency) when evaluating candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number, frequency, and withholding the award
rubrics_metrics.description: One Theodor Seuss Geisel Award for one book will be announced in January of each year ... If a suitable candidate is not found for any given year, the award will not be presented that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is annual but may be withheld if no entry meets the 'distinguished' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline and eligibility period
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline for award entries is December 31. The committee will consider books for the award up to and including this date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nomination deadlines may be adjusted depending on Midwinter Meeting dates and will be specified yearly; books must be published in the preceding year and submitted by Dec 31 of that publication year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedure and logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: How to submit: Complete the award submission form; Mail one copy of the book to the award committee chair; The deadline for submitting works is December 31 of the publication year; ALSC membership is not a requirement; There is no entry fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one copy is requested even if submitting for multiple awards; attach an optional cover letter with contact information; ALSC office/committee chair cannot confirm receipt — use tracking if confirmation is desired; in-person drop-offs to ALSC are not accepted; ALSC office cannot advise eligibility — submitters must review terms and criteria themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility determination confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility is determined by the committee and is confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should not expect public eligibility rulings from the ALSC office; the committee makes confidential eligibility decisions during deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee composition and appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The President ... will appoint the committee to administer the award. Membership shall be one chair and six members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee makeup is specified; committee resources and manuals are provided for members (manual, videos, FAQs).
